title: A day on Venus is longer than its year
body: Venus spins so slowly that one turn takes about 243 Earth days, but it goes around the Sun in about 225 days. So a day there is longer than a year.

title: Saturn would float
body: Saturn is mostly gas and its average density is lower than water’s. If you could find a bath big enough, Saturn would float.

title: The Sun is almost everything
body: The Sun holds about 99.8% of all the mass in the solar system. All the planets, moons and asteroids together make up the remaining 0.2%.

title: Astronauts grow taller in space
body: With no gravity squashing the spine, an astronaut can grow a few centimetres taller in space. Back on Earth they shrink to their normal height again.

title: Mars is red because it is rusty
body: The soil and dust on Mars contain lots of iron oxide, the same thing as rust. That is why the planet looks red-orange, even from Earth.

title: The Moon is slowly leaving us
body: The Moon moves about 3.8 centimetres farther from the Earth every year, about as fast as your fingernails grow.

title: A storm bigger than Earth
body: Jupiter’s Great Red Spot is a giant storm that has been watched for well over 150 years. It is wider than the Earth, though it has been getting smaller.

title: Our home galaxy
body: The Milky Way, the galaxy that contains our Sun, has hundreds of billions of stars. Many of them have planets going around them.

title: Footprints that stay
body: There is no wind or rain on the Moon, so the footprints left by the Apollo astronauts in 1969 are expected to stay for a very long time.

title: Light from the past
body: When you look at a star you see light that left it long ago. Some stars you can see on a clear night are hundreds or even thousands of light-years away, so you are seeing the past.

title: Neutron stars are unbelievably dense
body: When some massive stars die, they leave behind a neutron star only about 20 km across. A teaspoon of its material would weigh billions of tonnes.
